1	"""Single-file SQL query layer.
2	
3	Public API:
4	
5	* :func:`query_file` -- run a ``SELECT ... FROM input [WHERE ...]`` query
6	  against one columnar file and return a :class:`~columnar_analytics.format.Table`
7	* :class:`QuerySyntaxError` -- lexical / grammatical errors
8	* :class:`QueryValidationError` -- unknown columns, wrong table name,
9	  type-incompatible comparisons, invalid aggregate use
10	
11	The accepted grammar (keywords case-insensitive)::
12	
13	    query       := SELECT select_item (',' select_item)*
14	                   FROM ident [WHERE expr] [GROUP BY ident (',' ident)*]
15	                   [ORDER BY order_item (',' order_item)*]
16	                   [LIMIT uint]
17	    select_item := '*' | ident | agg_name '(' ('*' | ident) ')'
18	                   | scalar_expr AS alias
19	    order_item  := (ident | agg_name '(' ('*' | ident) ')')
20	                   [ASC | DESC] [NULLS FIRST | NULLS LAST]
21	    expr       := or_expr
22	    or_expr     := and_expr (OR and_expr)*
23	    and_expr    := cmp_expr (AND cmp_expr)*
24	    cmp_expr    := not_factor (cmp_op not_factor)?
25	    not_factor  := NOT not_factor | postfix
26	    postfix     := scalar_expr (IS [NOT] NULL)?
27	    scalar_expr := term (('+' | '-') term)*
28	    term        := factor (('*' | '/') factor)*
29	    factor      := ('+' | '-') factor | atom
30	    atom        := '(' expr ')' | operand
31	    operand     := ident | literal
32	    literal     := TRUE | FALSE | [+-]? int64 | [+-]? finite float64
33	                   | single-quoted utf8
34	
35	The supported aggregates are ``COUNT(*)``, ``COUNT(ident)`` and
36	``SUM`` / ``AVG`` / ``MIN`` / ``MAX`` applied to one column.  Without
37	GROUP BY the projection may contain aggregate expressions only; with
38	GROUP BY it may additionally contain the grouped columns.  A bare ``*``
39	must not be mixed with aggregates or grouping.  Aggregates are not
40	allowed inside WHERE, may not be nested, and aliases are not supported
41	for bare columns or aggregate calls.
42	
43	Scalar arithmetic (parentheses, unary ``+``/``-``, binary ``+`` ``-``
44	``*`` ``/``; precedence: parentheses, unary, ``*``/``/``, ``+``/``-``)
45	is available over int64 / float64 columns and numeric literals in SELECT
46	and WHERE.  A computed SELECT expression must be named with ``AS`` (the
47	alias follows the usual identifier rules and must be unique among the
48	output names); bare columns and aggregate calls keep their existing
49	result names.  int64 ``+``/``-``/``*`` on two int64 operands yields
50	int64; any float64 operand or a division yields float64, and unary
51	operators preserve the operand type.  Any NULL operand makes the result
52	NULL; the output column is nullable iff a participating column is
53	nullable (pure constants are not).  int64 overflow, division by zero and
54	non-finite float64 results raise :class:`QueryValidationError`.  A
55	numeric expression used directly as a boolean condition is rejected with
56	:class:`QueryValidationError` as well.  Non-aggregate queries execute
57	WHERE, then compute the sort keys, stably sort, apply LIMIT and only
58	then evaluate the SELECT expressions, so filtered or truncated rows
59	never trigger division-by-zero or overflow in the projection.  ORDER BY
60	may name a SELECT alias (an alias shadows an input column of the same
61	name) and sorts on the expression's result type with the usual NULL
62	placement and stability rules.  Aggregate queries do not accept scalar
63	expressions: GROUP BY keys and aggregate arguments stay plain column
64	references, and mixing a scalar expression into an aggregate query
65	raises :class:`QueryValidationError`.
66	
67	Operator precedence (highest first) is NOT, comparison, AND, OR; IS [NOT]
68	NULL is a postfix of its scalar operand.  Comparison operands may be
69	column references, literals or scalar arithmetic expressions.  WHERE
70	follows SQL three-valued logic: a normal
71	comparison against NULL yields UNKNOWN, UNKNOWN propagates through the
72	logical operators, and only TRUE rows are returned.
73	
74	After WHERE, rows are grouped in GROUP BY column order (a NULL key forms
75	its own group); without an explicit ORDER BY groups come out in the order
76	of their first selected row.  ORDER BY may only name selected grouped
77	columns or selected aggregate expressions; ASC is the default, NULLs sort
78	last regardless of direction unless NULLS FIRST / NULLS LAST is given, and
79	groups equal on every sort key keep that first-row order.  LIMIT then
80	keeps the first N groups.  Without GROUP BY and aggregates an aggregate
81	query over zero selected rows still yields one output row (COUNT 0, the
82	other aggregates NULL); with GROUP BY it yields zero rows.
83	
84	Two-file queries (:func:`query_files`) add one equi-join to the grammar::
85	
86	    query := SELECT ... FROM left_table [join_kind JOIN right_table
87	             ON left_table.column = right_table.column] ...
88	    join_kind := INNER | LEFT
89	
90	``sources`` maps table names to file paths; only the tables referenced by
91	the statement are read.  Aliases, compound ON conditions, other join types
92	and a second join are rejected as syntax errors before any file is opened.
93	In a join query every column reference outside ``COUNT(*)`` must be
94	qualified as ``table.column`` (either part may be a double-quoted
95	identifier).  ``SELECT *`` emits the left schema followed by the right
96	schema with ``table.column`` names; explicit projections keep their
97	qualified names and aggregates keep the uppercase ``FUNC(table.column)``
98	labels.  Join keys may share a type or mix int64 with float64; NULL keys
99	never match.  INNER JOIN emits every matching combination, LEFT JOIN also
100	emits unmatched left rows with the right-side values set to NULL (the
101	right result columns are nullable).  Rows expand in left-file order, and
102	within one left row in right-file order, before WHERE / GROUP BY /
103	ORDER BY / LIMIT apply with their usual semantics.
104	"""
105	
106	from __future__ import annotations
107	
108	import math
109	import os
110	import re
111	from collections.abc import Mapping
112	from dataclasses import dataclass
113	from functools import cmp_to_key
114	from typing import Any
115	
116	from .format import ColumnSchema, Schema, Table, read_file
117	
118	__all__ = [
119	    "QuerySyntaxError",
120	    "QueryValidationError",
121	    "query_file",
122	    "query_files",
123	]
124	
125	_KEYWORDS = frozenset(
126	    (
127	        "select",
128	        "from",
129	        "where",
130	        "as",
131	        "not",
132	        "and",
133	        "or",
134	        "is",
135	        "null",
136	        "true",
137	        "false",
138	        "order",
139	        "by",
140	        "asc",
141	        "desc",
142	        "nulls",
143	        "first",
144	        "last",
145	        "limit",
146	        "group",
147	        "inner",
148	        "left",
149	        "join",
150	        "on",
151	    )
152	)
153	
154	# Aggregate function names are ordinary (case-insensitive) identifiers that
155	# gain call syntax only in the projection and ORDER BY.
156	_AGG_NAMES = frozenset(("count", "sum", "avg", "min", "max"))
157	_INT64_MIN = -(2**63)
158	_INT64_MAX = 2**63 - 1
159	
160	
161	class QuerySyntaxError(Exception):
162	    """Raised when a query is lexically or grammatically invalid."""
163	
164	
165	class QueryValidationError(Exception):
166	    """Raised when a syntactically valid query is incompatible with the schema."""
167	
168	
169	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
170	# Tokeniser
171	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
172	
173	
174	@dataclass(frozen=True)
175	class _Token:
176	    kind: str  # one of: keyword, ident, number, string, op, star, eof
177	    value: Any
178	    text: str
179	
180	
181	_NUMBER_RE = re.compile(
182	    r"""
183	    \d+(?:\.\d*)?(?:[eE][+-]?\d+)?   # 1, 1., 1.5, 1e3, 1.5e-2
184	    | \.\d+(?:[eE][+-]?\d+)?         # .5
185	    """,
186	    re.VERBOSE,
187	)
188	# Bare identifiers: Unicode letters/underscore first, then word characters.
189	_IDENT_RE = re.compile(r"[^\W\d]\w*", re.UNICODE)
190	
191	
192	def _tokenize(sql: str) -> list[_Token]:
193	    if not isinstance(sql, str):
194	        raise QuerySyntaxError("SQL statement must be a string")
195	    tokens: list[_Token] = []
196	    i = 0
197	    n = len(sql)
198	    while i < n:
199	        ch = sql[i]
200	        if ch.isspace():
201	            i += 1
202	            continue
203	        if ch == "*":
204	            tokens.append(_Token("star", None, ch))
205	            i += 1
206	            continue
207	        if ch in ",()+-/":
208	            tokens.append(_Token("op", ch, ch))
209	            i += 1
210	            continue
211	        if ch in "=<>!":
212	            if ch == "!" and i + 1 < n and sql[i + 1] == "=":
213	                tokens.append(_Token("op", "!=", "!="))
214	                i += 2
215	                continue
216	            if ch in "<>" and i + 1 < n and sql[i + 1] == "=":
217	                op = ch + "="
218	                tokens.append(_Token("op", op, op))
219	                i += 2
220	                continue
221	            if ch in "=<>":
222	                tokens.append(_Token("op", ch, ch))
223	                i += 1
224	                continue
225	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"unexpected character '!' at position {i}")
226	        if ch == "'":
227	            value, new_i = _tokenize_string(sql, i)
228	            tokens.append(_Token("string", value, sql[i:new_i]))
229	            i = new_i
230	            continue
231	        if ch == '"':
232	            value, new_i = _tokenize_quoted_ident(sql, i)
233	            tokens.append(_token_from_word(value, quoted=True))
234	            i = new_i
235	            continue
236	        if ch.isdigit() or ch == ".":
237	            match = _NUMBER_RE.match(sql, i)
238	            if match:
239	                text = match.group(0)
240	                tokens.append(_Token("number", _parse_number(text), text))
241	                i = match.end()
242	                continue
243	            # A '.' that does not start a number is the qualifier separator
244	            # used by two-table queries ("table.column").
245	            tokens.append(_Token("op", ".", ch))
246	            i += 1
247	            continue
248	        match = _IDENT_RE.match(sql, i)
249	        if match:
250	            text = match.group(0)
251	            tokens.append(_token_from_word(text, quoted=False))
252	            i = match.end()
253	            continue
254	        raise QuerySyntaxError(f"unexpected character {ch!r} at position {i}")
255	    tokens.append(_Token("eof", None, ""))
256	    return tokens
257	
258	
259	def _token_from_word(word: str, *, quoted: bool) -> _Token:
260	    lowered = word.lower()
261	    if not quoted and lowered in _KEYWORDS:
262	        if lowered == "true":
263	            return _Token("number", True, word)
264	        if lowered == "false":
265	            return _Token("number", False, word)
266	        return _Token("keyword", lowered, word)
267	    return _Token("qident" if quoted else "ident", word, word)
268	
269	
270	def _tokenize_string(sql: str, start: int) -> tuple[str, int]:
271	    parts: list[str] = []
272	    i = start + 1
273	    n = len(sql)
274	    while True:
275	        j = sql.find("'", i)
276	        if j == -1:
277	            raise QuerySyntaxError("unterminated string literal")
278	        parts.append(sql[i:j])
279	        if j + 1 < n and sql[j + 1] == "'":
280	            parts.append("'")
281	            i = j + 2
282	            continue
283	        value = "".join(parts)
284	        try:
285	            value.encode("utf-8")
286	        except UnicodeEncodeError:
287	            raise QuerySyntaxError("string literal is not valid UTF-8") from None
288	        return value, j + 1
289	
290	
291	def _tokenize_quoted_ident(sql: str, start: int) -> tuple[str, int]:
292	    parts: list[str] = []
293	    i = start + 1
294	    n = len(sql)
295	    while True:
296	        j = sql.find('"', i)
297	        if j == -1:
298	            raise QuerySyntaxError("unterminated quoted identifier")
299	        parts.append(sql[i:j])
300	        if j + 1 < n and sql[j + 1] == '"':
301	            parts.append('"')
302	            i = j + 2
303	            continue
304	        value = "".join(parts)
305	        if not value:
306	            raise QuerySyntaxError("quoted identifier must not be empty")
307	        return value, j + 1
308	
309	
310	def _parse_number(text: str) -> int | float:
311	    try:
312	        if any(ch in text for ch in ".eE"):
313	            value: int | float = float(text)
314	        else:
315	            value = int(text, 10)
316	    except ValueError:
317	        raise QuerySyntaxError(f"invalid numeric literal {text!r}") from None
318	    if isinstance(value, int):
319	        # The magnitude 2**63 is accepted unsigned; the signed range check
320	        # happens after the optional leading sign is applied.
321	        if not (0 <= value <= 2**63):
322	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"integer literal {text} is outside the int64 range")
323	        return value
324	    if not math.isfinite(value):
325	        raise QuerySyntaxError(f"float literal {text} must be finite")
326	    return value
327	
328	
329	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
330	# Parsed expression tree
331	#
332	# Node tuples:
333	#   ("literal", python_value, type_name)
334	#   ("column", name, table|None, table_quoted)        -- as parsed
335	#   ("column", name, index, type_name, nullable)      -- after binding
336	#   ("arith", op, left_node, right_node)              -- as parsed (+ - * /)
337	#   ("arith", op, left_node, right_node, type_name)   -- after binding
338	#   ("unary", operand, negate)                        -- as parsed
339	#   ("unary", operand, negate, type_name)             -- after binding
340	#   ("cmp", op, left_node, right_node)
341	#   ("isnull", operand, negate)
342	#   ("not", operand)
343	#   ("and"|"or", left, right)
344	# Predicate nodes are boolean-typed (three-valued at evaluation time);
345	# "literal"/"column"/"arith"/"unary" nodes are value nodes.
346	#
347	# Projection / ORDER BY reference items:
348	#   ("column_ref", name)                 -- a plain column name
349	#   ("agg", func_upper, arg_name|None)   -- an aggregate call; arg None = '*'
350	#   ("expr", alias)                      -- a computed scalar expression
351	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
352	
353	
354	@dataclass(frozen=True)
355	class _RefItem:
356	    """One projection element or ORDER BY key as parsed."""
357	
358	    kind: str  # "star" | "column" | "agg" | "expr"
359	    name: str | None = None  # column name, or the AS alias for kind == "expr"
360	    func: str | None = None  # uppercase function name for kind == "agg"
361	    arg: str | None = None  # aggregate column argument; "" stands for '*'
362	    expr: tuple | None = None  # parsed scalar expression for kind == "expr"
363	    descending: bool = False
364	    nulls_first: bool | None = None  # None -> default (NULLs last)
365	    # Table qualifiers (two-table queries only; None when unqualified):
366	    table: str | None = None
367	    table_quoted: bool = False
368	    arg_table: str | None = None
369	    arg_table_quoted: bool = False
370	
371	
372	@dataclass(frozen=True)
373	class _Join:
374	    """The single optional equi-join of a two-table query."""
375	
376	    kind: str  # "inner" | "left"
377	    table: str  # right table name as spelled
378	    table_quoted: bool
379	    left_key: tuple  # (table, table_quoted, column)
380	    right_key: tuple  # (table, table_quoted, column)
381	
382	
383	@dataclass
384	class _Select:
385	    items: tuple[_RefItem, ...]  # projection; may be a single ("star",) item
386	    table: str
387	    table_quoted: bool
388	    where: tuple | None
389	    # GROUP BY entries are (table|None, table_quoted, name) triples.
390	    group_by: tuple[tuple, ...] | None
391	    order_by: tuple[_RefItem, ...] | None
392	    limit: int | None
393	    join: _Join | None = None
394	
395	    @property
396	    def star(self) -> bool:
397	        return len(self.items) == 1 and self.items[0].kind == "star"
398	
399	    @property
400	    def has_aggregate(self) -> bool:
401	        return any(item.kind == "agg" for item in self.items)
402	
403	    @property
404	    def is_aggregate_query(self) -> bool:
405	        return self.has_aggregate or self.group_by is not None
406	
407	
408	class _Parser:
409	    _CMP_OPS = frozenset(("=", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">="))
410	
411	    def __init__(self, tokens: list[_Token], allow_join: bool = False):
412	        self.tokens = tokens
413	        self.pos = 0
414	        # Two-table statements (qualified names + one JOIN clause) are only
415	        # enabled for query_files; single-file entry points keep rejecting
416	        # them as syntax errors.
417	        self._allow_join = allow_join
418	
419	    def parse(self) -> _Select:
420	        select = self._parse_select()
421	        if self._peek().kind != "eof":
422	            tok = self._peek()
423	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"unexpected trailing input {tok.text!r}")
424	        return select
425	
426	    def _parse_select(self) -> _Select:
427	        self._expect_keyword("select")
428	        items = tuple(self._parse_projection())
429	        self._expect_keyword("from")
430	        table_tok = self._expect_table_name()
431	        join = None
432	        if self._allow_join:
433	            if self._accept_keyword("inner"):
434	                self._expect_keyword("join")
435	                join = self._parse_join("inner")
436	            elif self._accept_keyword("left"):
437	                self._expect_keyword("join")
438	                join = self._parse_join("left")
439	        where = None
440	        if self._accept_keyword("where"):
441	            where = self._parse_or()
442	        group_by = None
443	        if self._accept_keyword("group"):
444	            self._expect_keyword("by")
445	            names = [self._parse_group_name()]
446	            while self._accept_op(","):
447	                names.append(self._parse_group_name())
448	            group_by = tuple(names)
449	        order_by = None
450	        if self._accept_keyword("order"):
451	            self._expect_keyword("by")
452	            order_items = [self._parse_order_item()]
453	            while self._accept_op(","):
454	                order_items.append(self._parse_order_item())
455	            order_by = tuple(order_items)
456	        limit = None
457	        if self._accept_keyword("limit"):
458	            limit = self._parse_limit()
459	        return _Select(
460	            items=items,
461	            table=table_tok.value,
462	            table_quoted=table_tok.kind == "qident",
463	            where=where,
464	            group_by=group_by,
465	            order_by=order_by,
466	            limit=limit,
467	            join=join,
468	        )
469	
470	    def _parse_join(self, kind: str) -> _Join:
471	        table_tok = self._expect_table_name()
472	        self._expect_keyword("on")
473	        left_key = self._parse_on_key()
474	        self._expect_op("=")
475	        right_key = self._parse_on_key()
476	        return _Join(
477	            kind=kind,
478	            table=table_tok.value,
479	            table_quoted=table_tok.kind == "qident",
480	            left_key=left_key,
481	            right_key=right_key,
482	        )
483	
484	    def _parse_on_key(self) -> tuple:
485	        tok = self._peek()
486	        if tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
487	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
488	                f"ON requires table-qualified columns, got {tok.text!r}"
489	            )
490	        self._next()
491	        if not self._accept_op("."):
492	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
493	                "ON requires table-qualified columns (table.column)"
494	            )
495	        nxt = self._peek()
496	        if nxt.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
497	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
498	                f"expected column name after '.' in ON, got {nxt.text!r}"
499	            )
500	        self._next()
501	        return (tok.value, tok.kind == "qident", nxt.value)
502	
503	    def _parse_projection(self) -> list[_RefItem]:
504	        items = [self._parse_select_item()]
505	        while self._accept_op(","):
506	            items.append(self._parse_select_item())
507	        # Aliases are only supported for computed scalar expressions (which
508	        # consume their own "AS alias" in _parse_select_item); a trailing
509	        # identifier (including the spelling "as") where FROM is expected
510	        # names one on a bare column or aggregate.  Plain queries keep their
511	        # historical QuerySyntaxError classification; aggregate queries treat
512	        # the unsupported alias as a validation error.
513	        tok = self._peek()
514	        if tok.kind in ("ident", "qident") or (
515	            tok.kind == "keyword" and tok.value == "as"
516	        ):
517	            grouped_ahead = any(
518	                t.kind == "keyword" and t.value == "group"
519	                for t in self.tokens[self.pos :]
520	            )
521	            if any(item.kind == "agg" for item in items) or grouped_ahead:
522	                raise QueryValidationError(
523	                    f"aliases are not supported; unexpected {tok.text!r} after projection item"
524	                )
525	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"expected FROM, got {tok.text!r}")
526	        return items
527	
528	    def _parse_select_item(self) -> _RefItem:
529	        tok = self._peek()
530	        if tok.kind == "star":
531	            self._next()
532	            return _RefItem("star")
533	        if (
534	            tok.kind == "ident"
535	            and tok.value.lower() in _AGG_NAMES
536	            and self.tokens[self.pos + 1].kind == "op"
537	            and self.tokens[self.pos + 1].value == "("
538	        ):
539	            item = self._parse_column_or_agg()
540	            if self._arith_op_ahead():
541	                raise QueryValidationError(
542	                    "aggregate calls cannot be combined with scalar arithmetic"
543	                )
544	            return item
545	        node = self._parse_arith()
546	        if node[0] == "column":
547	            # A bare (possibly parenthesised) column reference keeps its
548	            # existing projection behaviour and needs no alias.
549	            return _RefItem(
550	                "column", name=node[1], table=node[2], table_quoted=node[3]
551	            )
552	        # A computed scalar expression must be named with AS.
553	        self._expect_keyword("as")
554	        alias = self._peek()
555	        if alias.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
556	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
557	                f"AS requires a result name, got {alias.text!r}"
558	            )
559	        self._next()
560	        return _RefItem("expr", name=alias.value, expr=node)
561	
562	    def _arith_op_ahead(self) -> bool:
563	        tok = self._peek()
564	        return tok.kind == "star" or (
565	            tok.kind == "op" and tok.value in ("+", "-", "/")
566	        )
567	
568	    def _parse_order_item(self) -> _RefItem:
569	        item = self._parse_column_or_agg()
570	        descending = False
571	        if self._accept_keyword("asc"):
572	            descending = False
573	        elif self._accept_keyword("desc"):
574	            descending = True
575	        nulls_first: bool | None = None
576	        if self._accept_keyword("nulls"):
577	            if self._accept_keyword("first"):
578	                nulls_first = True
579	            elif self._accept_keyword("last"):
580	                nulls_first = False
581	            else:
582	                tok = self._peek()
583	                raise QuerySyntaxError(
584	                    f"expected FIRST or LAST after NULLS, got {tok.text!r}"
585	                )
586	        return _RefItem(
587	            item.kind,
588	            name=item.name,
589	            func=item.func,
590	            arg=item.arg,
591	            descending=descending,
592	            nulls_first=nulls_first,
593	            table=item.table,
594	            table_quoted=item.table_quoted,
595	            arg_table=item.arg_table,
596	            arg_table_quoted=item.arg_table_quoted,
597	        )
598	
599	    def _qualifier_ahead(self) -> bool:
600	        nxt = self.tokens[self.pos + 1]
601	        return nxt.kind == "op" and nxt.value == "."
602	
603	    def _parse_qualified_column(self) -> _RefItem:
604	        # Current token starts "table.column"; consumes all three tokens.
605	        table_tok = self._next()
606	        self._expect_op(".")
607	        name_tok = self._peek()
608	        if name_tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
609	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
610	                f"expected identifier after '.', got {name_tok.text!r}"
611	            )
612	        self._next()
613	        return _RefItem(
614	            "column",
615	            name=name_tok.value,
616	            table=table_tok.value,
617	            table_quoted=table_tok.kind == "qident",
618	        )
619	
620	    def _parse_column_or_agg(self) -> _RefItem:
621	        tok = self._peek()
622	        if tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
623	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"expected identifier, got {tok.text!r}")
624	        if self._allow_join and self._qualifier_ahead():
625	            return self._parse_qualified_column()
626	        # A quoted identifier, or a bare word not spelled like an aggregate,
627	        # can only be a plain column reference.
628	        if tok.kind == "qident" or tok.value.lower() not in _AGG_NAMES:
629	            self._next()
630	            return _RefItem("column", name=tok.value)
631	        func = tok.value.lower()
632	        self._next()  # consume the function name
633	        if not self._accept_op("("):
634	            # e.g. a column literally named "count" -- the name token is
635	            # already consumed, so it is a plain column reference.
636	            return _RefItem("column", name=tok.value)
637	        arg, arg_table, arg_table_quoted = self._parse_aggregate_args(func)
638	        self._expect_op(")")
639	        return _RefItem(
640	            "agg",
641	            func=func.upper(),
642	            arg=arg,
643	            arg_table=arg_table,
644	            arg_table_quoted=arg_table_quoted,
645	        )
646	
647	    def _parse_aggregate_args(self, func: str) -> tuple:
648	        # Exactly one argument: '*' for COUNT, otherwise one (possibly
649	        # table-qualified) identifier.  Returns (name, table, table_quoted);
650	        # name "" stands for '*'.
651	        tok = self._peek()
652	        if tok.kind == "star":
653	            if func != "count":
654	                raise QuerySyntaxError(f"{func.upper()} does not accept '*'")
655	            self._next()
656	            return ("", None, False)
657	        if tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
658	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
659	                f"{func.upper()} requires one column argument, got {tok.text!r}"
660	            )
661	        if self._allow_join and self._qualifier_ahead():
662	            item = self._parse_qualified_column()
663	            nxt = self._peek()
664	            if nxt.kind == "op" and nxt.value == "(":
665	                raise QuerySyntaxError(
666	                    f"{func.upper()} argument must be a column name, not a function call"
667	                )
668	            self._reject_expression_in_agg_arg(func)
669	            return (item.name, item.table, item.table_quoted)
670	        self._next()
671	        nxt = self._peek()
672	        if nxt.kind == "op" and nxt.value == "(":
673	            if tok.kind == "ident" and tok.value.lower() in _AGG_NAMES:
674	                raise QueryValidationError(
675	                    f"aggregate functions must not be nested: "
676	                    f"{func.upper()}({tok.value.upper()}(...))"
677	                )
678	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
679	                f"{func.upper()} argument must be a column name, not a function call"
680	            )
681	        self._reject_expression_in_agg_arg(func)
682	        return (tok.value, None, False)
683	
684	    def _reject_expression_in_agg_arg(self, func: str) -> None:
685	        # Aggregate arguments stay limited to plain column references; a
686	        # scalar expression inside an aggregate query is a validation error.
687	        if self._arith_op_ahead():
688	            raise QueryValidationError(
689	                f"{func.upper()} argument must be a column reference, not an expression"
690	            )
691	
692	    def _parse_limit(self) -> int:
693	        tok = self._peek()
694	        if (
695	            tok.kind != "number"
696	            or isinstance(tok.value, bool)
697	            or not isinstance(tok.value, int)
698	        ):
699	            raise QuerySyntaxError("LIMIT requires an unsigned integer literal")
700	        self._next()
701	        if not (0 <= tok.value <= 2**63 - 1):
702	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
703	                f"LIMIT value {tok.value} is outside the allowed range"
704	            )
705	        return tok.value
706	
707	    def _expect_table_name(self) -> _Token:
708	        tok = self._peek()
709	        if tok.kind in ("ident", "qident"):
710	            return self._next()
711	        raise QuerySyntaxError(f"expected table name, got {tok.text!r}")
712	
713	    def _parse_group_name(self) -> tuple:
714	        # Returns a (table|None, table_quoted, name) triple.
715	        tok = self._peek()
716	        if tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
717	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"expected identifier, got {tok.text!r}")
718	        if self._allow_join and self._qualifier_ahead():
719	            item = self._parse_qualified_column()
720	            result = (item.table, item.table_quoted, item.name)
721	        else:
722	            self._next()
723	            result = (None, False, tok.value)
724	        # GROUP BY keeps accepting column references only; a scalar
725	        # expression in an aggregate query is a validation error.
726	        if self._arith_op_ahead():
727	            raise QueryValidationError(
728	                "GROUP BY only accepts column references, not expressions"
729	            )
730	        return result
731	
732	    # WHERE expression grammar ------------------------------------------------
733	
734	    def _parse_or(self) -> tuple:
735	        node = self._parse_and()
736	        while self._accept_keyword("or"):
737	            node = ("or", node, self._parse_and())
738	        return node
739	
740	    def _parse_and(self) -> tuple:
741	        node = self._parse_comparison()
742	        while self._accept_keyword("and"):
743	            node = ("and", node, self._parse_comparison())
744	        return node
745	
746	    def _parse_comparison(self) -> tuple:
747	        left = self._parse_not_factor()
748	        tok = self._peek()
749	        if tok.kind == "op" and tok.value in self._CMP_OPS:
750	            self._next()
751	            right = self._parse_not_factor()
752	            return ("cmp", tok.value, left, right)
753	        return left
754	
755	    def _parse_not_factor(self) -> tuple:
756	        if self._accept_keyword("not"):
757	            return ("not", self._parse_not_factor())
758	        return self._parse_postfix()
759	
760	    def _parse_postfix(self) -> tuple:
761	        node = self._parse_arith()
762	        if self._accept_keyword("is"):
763	            negate = self._accept_keyword("not")
764	            self._expect_keyword("null")
765	            node = ("isnull", node, negate)
766	        return node
767	
768	    # Arithmetic expressions (numeric scalar operands) ------------------------
769	    # Precedence (highest first): parentheses, unary +/-, * /, + -.
770	
771	    def _parse_arith(self) -> tuple:
772	        node = self._parse_term()
773	        while True:
774	            tok = self._peek()
775	            if tok.kind == "op" and tok.value in ("+", "-"):
776	                self._next()
777	                node = ("arith", tok.value, node, self._parse_term())
778	            else:
779	                return node
780	
781	    def _parse_term(self) -> tuple:
782	        node = self._parse_factor()
783	        while True:
784	            tok = self._peek()
785	            if tok.kind == "star":
786	                self._next()
787	                node = ("arith", "*", node, self._parse_factor())
788	            elif tok.kind == "op" and tok.value == "/":
789	                self._next()
790	                node = ("arith", "/", node, self._parse_factor())
791	            else:
792	                return node
793	
794	    def _parse_factor(self) -> tuple:
795	        tok = self._peek()
796	        if tok.kind == "op" and tok.value in ("+", "-"):
797	            negate = tok.value == "-"
798	            self._next()
799	            nxt = self._peek()
800	            if nxt.kind == "number" and not isinstance(nxt.value, bool):
801	                # A signed numeric literal is folded at parse time so the
802	                # signed int64 range check keeps its historical meaning
803	                # (-9223372036854775808 is valid, the bare magnitude is not).
804	                self._next()
805	                value = nxt.value
806	                if isinstance(value, int):
807	                    if negate:
808	                        value = -value
809	                    if not (-(2**63) <= value <= 2**63 - 1):
810	                        raise QuerySyntaxError(
811	                            "integer literal is outside the int64 range"
812	                        )
813	                    return ("literal", value, "int64")
814	                if negate:
815	                    value = -value
816	                return ("literal", value, "float64")
817	            if nxt.kind not in ("ident", "qident") and not (
818	                nxt.kind == "op" and nxt.value == "("
819	            ):
820	                raise QuerySyntaxError(
821	                    "sign must be followed by a numeric literal or expression"
822	                )
823	            return ("unary", self._parse_factor(), negate)
824	        node = self._parse_atom()
825	        if (
826	            node[0] == "literal"
827	            and isinstance(node[1], int)
828	            and not isinstance(node[1], bool)
829	            and node[1] > 2**63 - 1
830	        ):
831	            # The magnitude 2**63 is only reachable through an explicit
832	            # negation; a bare literal must fit the signed int64 range.
833	            raise QuerySyntaxError("integer literal is outside the int64 range")
834	        return node
835	
836	    def _parse_atom(self) -> tuple:
837	        if self._accept_op("("):
838	            node = self._parse_or()
839	            self._expect_op(")")
840	            return node
841	        tok = self._peek()
842	        if tok.kind == "number":
843	            self._next()
844	            value = tok.value
845	            if isinstance(value, bool):
846	                return ("literal", value, "bool")
847	            type_name = "int64" if isinstance(value, int) else "float64"
848	            return ("literal", value, type_name)
849	        if tok.kind == "string":
850	            self._next()
851	            return ("literal", tok.value, "utf8")
852	        if tok.kind in ("ident", "qident"):
853	            if self._allow_join and self._qualifier_ahead():
854	                item = self._parse_qualified_column()
855	                return ("column", item.name, item.table, item.table_quoted)
856	            nxt = self.tokens[self.pos + 1]
857	            if (
858	                tok.kind == "ident"
859	                and tok.value.lower() in _AGG_NAMES
860	                and nxt.kind == "op"
861	                and nxt.value == "("
862	            ):
863	                raise QueryValidationError(
864	                    f"aggregate {tok.value.upper()}(...) is not allowed here"
865	                )
866	            self._next()
867	            return ("column", tok.value, None, False)
868	        if tok.kind == "keyword":
869	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"unexpected keyword {tok.text.upper()!r} in expression")
870	        raise QuerySyntaxError(f"unexpected token {tok.text!r} in expression")
871	
872	    # Token helpers -----------------------------------------------------------
873	
874	    def _peek(self) -> _Token:
875	        return self.tokens[self.pos]
876	
877	    def _next(self) -> _Token:
878	        tok = self.tokens[self.pos]
879	        self.pos += 1
880	        return tok
881	
882	    def _accept(self, kind: str) -> bool:
883	        if self._peek().kind == kind:
884	            self.pos += 1
885	            return True
886	        return False
887	
888	    def _accept_op(self, value: str) -> bool:
889	        tok = self._peek()
890	        if tok.kind == "op" and tok.value == value:
891	            self.pos += 1
892	            return True
893	        return False
894	
895	    def _accept_keyword(self, value: str) -> bool:
896	        tok = self._peek()
897	        if tok.kind == "keyword" and tok.value == value:
898	            self.pos += 1
899	            return True
900	        return False
901	
902	    def _expect_keyword(self, value: str) -> _Token:
903	        tok = self._peek()
904	        if tok.kind != "keyword" or tok.value != value:
905	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"expected {value.upper()}, got {tok.text!r}")
906	        return self._next()
907	
908	    def _expect_op(self, value: str) -> _Token:
909	        tok = self._peek()
910	        if tok.kind != "op" or tok.value != value:
911	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"expected {value!r}, got {tok.text!r}")
912	        return self._next()

920	@dataclass(frozen=True)
921	class _BoundItem:
922	    """A validated projection element."""
923	
924	    kind: str  # "column" | "agg" | "expr"
925	    output_name: str
926	    # kind == "column":
927	    col_index: int = -1
928	    # kind == "agg":
929	    func: str = ""
930	    arg_index: int = -1  # -1 means COUNT(*)
931	    arg_type: str = ""
932	    # kind == "expr":
933	    expr: tuple | None = None  # bound scalar expression
934	    out_type: str = ""
935	    nullable: bool = True
936	
937	
938	def _bind_select(select: _Select, schema: Schema, expected_table="input") -> dict:

1263	def _bind_expr(node: tuple, schema: Schema) -> tuple:
1264	    tag = node[0]
1265	    if tag == "literal":
1266	        return node
1267	    if tag == "column":
1268	        name = node[1]
1269	        try:
1270	            index = schema.index(name)
1271	        except KeyError:
1272	            raise QueryValidationError(f"unknown column: {name!r}") from None
1273	        col = schema.columns[index]
1274	        return ("column", name, index, col.type, col.nullable)
1275	    if tag == "not":
1276	        operand = _bind_expr(node[1], schema)
1277	        _require_boolean(operand, "NOT")
1278	        return ("not", operand)
1279	    if tag in ("and", "or"):
1280	        left = _bind_expr(node[1], schema)
1281	        right = _bind_expr(node[2], schema)
1282	        _require_boolean(left, tag.upper())
1283	        _require_boolean(right, tag.upper())
1284	        return (tag, left, right)
1285	    if tag == "isnull":
1286	        operand = _bind_expr(node[1], schema)
1287	        if operand[0] not in ("literal", "column", "arith", "unary"):
1288	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
1289	                "IS NULL operand must be a column reference or a literal"
1290	            )
1291	        return ("isnull", operand, node[2])
1292	    if tag == "unary":
1293	        operand = _bind_expr(node[1], schema)
1294	        type_name = _expr_type(operand)
1295	        if type_name not in ("int64", "float64"):
1296	            raise QueryValidationError(
1297	                f"unary +/- requires a numeric operand, got {type_name}"
1298	            )
1299	        return ("unary", operand, node[2], type_name)
1300	    if tag == "arith":
1301	        left = _bind_expr(node[2], schema)
1302	        right = _bind_expr(node[3], schema)
1303	        left_t = _expr_type(left)
1304	        right_t = _expr_type(right)
1305	        if left_t not in ("int64", "float64") or right_t not in ("int64", "float64"):
1306	            raise QueryValidationError(
1307	                f"arithmetic requires numeric operands, got {left_t} and {right_t}"
1308	            )
1309	        op = node[1]
1310	        out_type = (
1311	            "float64"
1312	            if op == "/" or "float64" in (left_t, right_t)

1314	        )

1350	        return node[2]
1351	    if tag == "column":
1352	        return node[3]
1353	    if tag == "unary":

1387	def _eval(node: tuple, row: tuple) -> bool | None:
1388	    tag = node[0]
1389	    if tag == "literal":
1390	        return node[1]
1391	    if tag == "column":
1392	        return row[node[2]]
1393	    if tag == "unary":
1394	        value = _eval(node[1], row)
1395	        if value is None:
1396	            return None
1397	        if not node[2]:  # unary plus keeps the value
1398	            return value
1399	        return _negate_value(value)
1400	    if tag == "arith":
1401	        left = _eval(node[2], row)
1402	        right = _eval(node[3], row)
1403	        if left is None or right is None:
1404	            return None
1405	        return _arith_value(node[1], left, right)
1406	    if tag == "isnull":
1407	        value = _eval(node[1], row)
1408	        result = value is None
1409	        return (not result) if node[2] else result
1410	    if tag == "not":
1411	        value = _eval(node[1], row)
1412	        return None if value is None else (not value)
1413	    if tag in ("and", "or"):
1414	        # Short-circuit SQL semantics; UNKNOWN propagates only when needed.
1415	        if tag == "and":
1416	            left = _eval(node[1], row)
1417	            if left is False:
1418	                return False
1419	            right = _eval(node[2], row)
1420	            if right is False:
1421	                return False
1422	            if left is None or right is None:
1423	                return None
1424	            return True
1425	        left = _eval(node[1], row)
1426	        if left is True:
1427	            return True
1428	        right = _eval(node[2], row)
1429	        if right is True:
1430	            return True
1431	        if left is None or right is None:
1432	            return None
1433	        return False
1434	    if tag == "cmp":
1435	        left = _eval(node[2], row)
1436	        right = _eval(node[3], row)
1437	        if left is None or right is None:
1438	            return None
1439	        op = node[1]
1440	        if op == "=":
1441	            result = left == right
1442	        elif op == "!=":
1443	            result = left != right
1444	        elif op == "<":
1445	            result = left < right
1446	        elif op == "<=":
1447	            result = left <= right
1448	        elif op == ">":
1449	            result = left > right
1450	        else:  # ">="
1451	            result = left >= right
1452	        return bool(result)
1453	    raise QuerySyntaxError(f"unsupported expression: {tag}")  # pragma: no cover

1456	def _negate_value(value):
1457	    # Unary minus: the type is preserved; only int64 can overflow.
1458	    if isinstance(value, int):
1459	        if value == _INT64_MIN:
1460	            raise QueryValidationError(
1461	                "negating the int64 minimum overflows the int64 range"
1462	            )
1463	        return -value
1464	    return -value

1467	def _arith_value(op: str, left, right):
1468	    # int64 op int64 stays int64 for + - *; any float64 operand or a
1469	    # division produces float64.  NULLs are handled by the caller.
1470	    if op == "/" or isinstance(left, float) or isinstance(right, float):
1471	        if op == "/" and right == 0:
1472	            raise QueryValidationError("division by zero")
1473	        a = float(left)
1474	        b = float(right)
1475	        if op == "+":
1476	            result = a + b
1477	        elif op == "-":
1478	            result = a - b
1479	        elif op == "*":
1480	            result = a * b
1481	        else:
1482	            result = a / b
1483	        if not math.isfinite(result):
1484	            raise QueryValidationError(
1485	                "float64 arithmetic produced a non-finite value"
1486	            )
1487	        return result
1488	    if op == "+":
1489	        result = left + right
1490	    elif op == "-":
1491	        result = left - right
1492	    else:
1493	        result = left * right
1494	    if not (_INT64_MIN <= result <= _INT64_MAX):
1495	        raise QueryValidationError("int64 arithmetic overflowed the int64 range")
1496	    return result

1506	        if arg_index == -1:
1507	            return len(rows)

1515	
1516	    if func == "MIN":

1518	    if func == "MAX":
1519	        return max(values)
1520	    if func == "SUM":
1521	        if arg_type == "int64":
1522	            # Python integers are unbounded; the int64 result is rejected only
1523	            # when the final total leaves the int64 range.
1524	            total = sum(values)
1525	            if not (_INT64_MIN <= total <= _INT64_MAX):
1526	                raise QueryValidationError("SUM overflowed the int64 range")
1527	            return total
1528	        try:
1529	            total = math.fsum(values)
1530	        except OverflowError:
1531	            raise QueryValidationError("SUM produced a non-finite float64 value") from None
1532	        if not math.isfinite(total):
1533	            raise QueryValidationError("SUM produced a non-finite float64 value")
1534	        return total
1535	    # AVG
1536	    try:
1537	        result = math.fsum(values) / len(values)
1538	    except OverflowError:
1539	        raise QueryValidationError("AVG produced a non-finite float64 value") from None
1540	    if not math.isfinite(result):
1541	        raise QueryValidationError("AVG produced a non-finite float64 value")
1542	    return result
1543	
1544	
1545	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
1546	# Public entry points
1547	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
1548

1550	def query_file(path: Any, sql: str) -> Table:
1551	    """Run ``sql`` against the single columnar file ``path``.
1552	
1553	    Returns a :class:`~columnar_analytics.format.Table` with columns in
1554	    projection order.  Rows are filtered by WHERE, then grouped (for
1555	    aggregate queries) or sorted by ORDER BY, then capped by LIMIT, then
1556	    projected; without ORDER BY the file's original row order (or the
1557	    first-selected-row group order) is kept.  The statement is parsed
1558	    before the file is touched, so purely grammatical errors surface as
1559	    :class:`QuerySyntaxError` regardless of whether ``path`` exists.
1560	    Unknown columns, duplicate result columns, the wrong table name,
1561	    type-incompatible predicates, ungrouped columns, illegal aggregate
1562	    arguments or int64 SUM overflow raise :class:`QueryValidationError`;
1563	    malformed files raise :class:`~columnar_analytics.format.ColumnarFormatError`;
1564	    other I/O failures propagate as :class:`OSError`.
1565	    """
1566	    tokens = _tokenize(sql)
1567	    select = _Parser(tokens).parse()
1568	    table = read_file(path)
1569	    return _run_query(table, select)
1570	
1571	
1572	def query_table(table: Table, sql: str) -> Table:
1573	    """Apply ``sql`` (``FROM input``) to an in-memory table."""
1574	    tokens = _tokenize(sql)
1575	    select = _Parser(tokens).parse()
1576	    return _run_query(table, select)
1577	
1578	
1579	def query_files(sources: Any, sql: str) -> Table:
1580	    """Run ``sql`` against the tables named by ``sources``.
1581	
1582	    ``sources`` maps table names to columnar file paths; only the tables
1583	    referenced by the statement are read.  The statement may join two of
1584	    them once (``INNER JOIN`` / ``LEFT JOIN ... ON t1.col = t2.col``); see
1585	    the module docstring for the exact grammar and semantics.
1586	
1587	    A non-mapping or empty ``sources``, non-string keys or non-path values
1588	    raise :class:`ValueError` before any file is touched.  Lexical and
1589	    grammatical errors (including join-keyword, ON and multiple-join
1590	    problems) raise :class:`QuerySyntaxError` before any file is read.
1591	    Unknown tables or columns, unqualified column references in a join
1592	    query, duplicate tables, misattributed or type-incompatible join keys
1593	    and duplicate result columns raise :class:`QueryValidationError`;
1594	    malformed files raise :class:`~columnar_analytics.format.ColumnarFormatError`;
1595	    other I/O failures propagate as :class:`OSError`.
1596	    """
1597	    paths = _validate_sources(sources)
1598	    tokens = _tokenize(sql)
1599	    select = _Parser(tokens, allow_join=True).parse()
1600	    left_key = _resolve_table_ref(select.table, select.table_quoted, tuple(paths))
1601	    if select.join is None:
1602	        rewritten = _rewrite_select(select, _single_table_resolver(left_key))
1603	        table = read_file(paths[left_key])
1604	        return _run_query(table, rewritten, expected_table=None)
1605	
1606	    join = select.join
1607	    right_key = _resolve_table_ref(join.table, join.table_quoted, tuple(paths))
1608	    if right_key == left_key:
1609	        raise QueryValidationError(f"duplicate table {right_key!r} in join")
1610	    on_left = _resolve_table_ref(join.left_key[0], join.left_key[1], (left_key, right_key))
1611	    on_right = _resolve_table_ref(join.right_key[0], join.right_key[1], (left_key, right_key))
1612	    if on_left != left_key or on_right != right_key:
1613	        raise QueryValidationError(
1614	            "ON keys must reference the left and right tables respectively"
1615	        )
1616	    # Qualifier checks (unqualified / unknown-table column references) do
1617	    # not need the files and run before any read.
1618	    rewritten = _rewrite_select(select, _join_resolver(left_key, right_key))
1619	    left_table = read_file(paths[left_key])
1620	    right_table = read_file(paths[right_key])
1621	    combined = _build_joined_table(left_key, left_table, right_key, right_table, join)
1622	    return _run_query(combined, rewritten, expected_table=None)
1623	
1624	
1625	def _validate_sources(sources: Any) -> dict:
1626	    if not isinstance(sources, Mapping):
1627	        raise ValueError("sources must be a mapping of table names to file paths")
1628	    if not sources:
1629	        raise ValueError("sources must not be empty")
1630	    paths = {}
1631	    for key, value in sources.items():
1632	        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
1633	            raise ValueError("sources keys must be non-empty strings")
1634	        if not isinstance(value, (str, os.PathLike)):
1635	            raise ValueError(f"sources[{key!r}] must be a file path")
1636	        paths[key] = value
1637	    return paths
1638	
1639	
1640	def _resolve_table_ref(name: str, quoted: bool, candidates: tuple) -> str:
1641	    """Resolve a table reference against the available canonical names.
1642	
1643	    Quoted references match exactly; bare references match exactly first,
1644	    then case-insensitively when that is unambiguous.
1645	    """
1646	    if name in candidates:
1647	        return name
1648	    if not quoted:
1649	        lowered = name.lower()
1650	        matches = [c for c in candidates if c.lower() == lowered]
1651	        if len(matches) == 1:
1652	            return matches[0]
1653	        if len(matches) > 1:
1654	            raise QueryValidationError(f"ambiguous table name {name!r}")
1655	    raise QueryValidationError(f"unknown table {name!r}")
1656	
1657	
1658	def _single_table_resolver(table_key: str):
1659	    def resolve(table, table_quoted, column):
1660	        if table is not None:
1661	            _resolve_table_ref(table, table_quoted, (table_key,))
1662	        return column
1663	
1664	    return resolve
1665	
1666	
1667	def _join_resolver(left_key: str, right_key: str):
1668	    def resolve(table, table_quoted, column):
1669	        if table is None:
1670	            raise QueryValidationError(
1671	                f"column reference {column!r} must be qualified with a table name"
1672	            )
1673	        key = _resolve_table_ref(table, table_quoted, (left_key, right_key))
1674	        return f"{key}.{column}"
1675	
1676	    return resolve
1677	
1678	
1679	def _rewrite_select(select: _Select, resolve) -> _Select:
1680	    """Resolve every column reference to its canonical output name."""
1681	    items = tuple(_rewrite_ref_item(item, resolve) for item in select.items)
1682	    # ORDER BY names that match a SELECT alias stay unresolved here; the
1683	    # binder resolves them against the aliased expressions first.
1684	    aliases = {item.name for item in items if item.kind == "expr"}
1685	    group_by = None
1686	    if select.group_by is not None:
1687	        group_by = tuple(
1688	            (None, False, resolve(table, quoted, name))
1689	            for table, quoted, name in select.group_by
1690	        )
1691	    order_by = None
1692	    if select.order_by is not None:
1693	        order_by = tuple(
1694	            item
1695	            if item.kind == "column" and item.table is None and item.name in aliases
1696	            else _rewrite_ref_item(item, resolve)
1697	            for item in select.order_by
1698	        )
1699	    where = _rewrite_expr(select.where, resolve) if select.where is not None else None
1700	    return _Select(
1701	        items=items,
1702	        table=select.table,
1703	        table_quoted=select.table_quoted,
1704	        where=where,
1705	        group_by=group_by,
1706	        order_by=order_by,
1707	        limit=select.limit,
1708	    )
1709	
1710	
1711	def _rewrite_ref_item(item: _RefItem, resolve) -> _RefItem:
1712	    if item.kind == "star":
1713	        return item
1714	    if item.kind == "expr":
1715	        return _RefItem(
1716	            "expr",
1717	            name=item.name,
1718	            expr=_rewrite_expr(item.expr, resolve),
1719	            descending=item.descending,
1720	            nulls_first=item.nulls_first,
1721	        )
1722	    if item.kind == "column":
1723	        return _RefItem(
1724	            "column",
1725	            name=resolve(item.table, item.table_quoted, item.name),
1726	            descending=item.descending,
1727	            nulls_first=item.nulls_first,
1728	        )
1729	    arg = item.arg
1730	    if arg:
1731	        arg = resolve(item.arg_table, item.arg_table_quoted, arg)
1732	    return _RefItem(
1733	        "agg",
1734	        func=item.func,
1735	        arg=arg,
1736	        descending=item.descending,
1737	        nulls_first=item.nulls_first,
1738	    )
1739	
1740	
1741	def _rewrite_expr(node: tuple, resolve) -> tuple:
1742	    tag = node[0]
1743	    if tag == "literal":
1744	        return node
1745	    if tag == "column":
1746	        return ("column", resolve(node[2], node[3], node[1]), None, False)
1747	    if tag == "unary":
1748	        return ("unary", _rewrite_expr(node[1], resolve), node[2])
1749	    if tag == "arith":
1750	        return ("arith", node[1], _rewrite_expr(node[2], resolve), _rewrite_expr(node[3], resolve))
1751	    if tag == "not":
1752	        return ("not", _rewrite_expr(node[1], resolve))
1753	    if tag in ("and", "or"):
1754	        return (tag, _rewrite_expr(node[1], resolve), _rewrite_expr(node[2], resolve))
1755	    if tag == "isnull":
1756	        return ("isnull", _rewrite_expr(node[1], resolve), node[2])
1757	    if tag == "cmp":
1758	        return ("cmp", node[1], _rewrite_expr(node[2], resolve), _rewrite_expr(node[3], resolve))
1759	    raise QuerySyntaxError(f"unsupported expression: {tag}")  # pragma: no cover - defensive
1760	
1761	
1762	def _build_joined_table(
1763	    left_key: str, left: Table, right_key: str, right: Table, join: _Join
1764	) -> Table:
1765	    left_col = join.left_key[2]
1766	    right_col = join.right_key[2]
1767	    try:
1768	        left_idx = left.schema.index(left_col)
1769	    except KeyError:
1770	        raise QueryValidationError(
1771	            f"unknown column: {f'{left_key}.{left_col}'!r}"
1772	        ) from None
1773	    try:
1774	        right_idx = right.schema.index(right_col)
1775	    except KeyError:
1776	        raise QueryValidationError(
1777	            f"unknown column: {f'{right_key}.{right_col}'!r}"
1778	        ) from None
1779	    left_type = left.schema.columns[left_idx].type
1780	    right_type = right.schema.columns[right_idx].type
1781	    if left_type != right_type and not {left_type, right_type} <= {"int64", "float64"}:
1782	        raise QueryValidationError(
1783	            f"join key types are incompatible: {left_type} and {right_type}"
1784	        )
1785	
1786	    # The combined schema is left columns then right columns, named
1787	    # "table.column"; a LEFT JOIN makes every right-side column nullable.
1788	    combined_columns = [
1789	        ColumnSchema(f"{left_key}.{col.name}", col.type, col.nullable)
1790	        for col in left.schema.columns
1791	    ] + [
1792	        ColumnSchema(
1793	            f"{right_key}.{col.name}",
1794	            col.type,
1795	            True if join.kind == "left" else col.nullable,
1796	        )
1797	        for col in right.schema.columns
1798	    ]
1799	    names = [col.name for col in combined_columns]
1800	    if len(set(names)) != len(names):
1801	        raise QueryValidationError("joined tables produce duplicate column names")
1802	    schema = Schema(combined_columns)
1803	    columns = _join_columns(left, right, left_idx, right_idx, join.kind)
1804	    return Table._from_storage(schema, columns)
1805	
1806	
1807	def _join_columns(
1808	    left: Table, right: Table, left_idx: int, right_idx: int, kind: str
1809	) -> list:
1810	    """Nested-loop equi-join preserving left-then-right file row order."""
1811	    left_cols = left._columns
1812	    right_cols = right._columns
1813	    left_width = len(left_cols)
1814	    right_width = len(right_cols)
1815	    # NULL keys never match, so they stay out of the right-side index.
1816	    index: dict[Any, list[int]] = {}
1817	    for j, key in enumerate(right_cols[right_idx]):
1818	        if key is not None:
1819	            index.setdefault(key, []).append(j)
1820	    out = [[] for _ in range(left_width + right_width)]
1821	    for i in range(left.row_count):
1822	        key = left_cols[left_idx][i]
1823	        matches = index.get(key) if key is not None else None
1824	        if matches:
1825	            for j in matches:
1826	                for c in range(left_width):
1827	                    out[c].append(left_cols[c][i])
1828	                for c in range(right_width):
1829	                    out[left_width + c].append(right_cols[c][j])
1830	        elif kind == "left":
1831	            for c in range(left_width):
1832	                out[c].append(left_cols[c][i])
1833	            for c in range(right_width):
1834	                out[left_width + c].append(None)
1835	    return out
1836	
1837	
1838	def _run_query(table: Table, select: _Select, expected_table="input") -> Table:
1839	    bound = _bind_select(select, table.schema, expected_table)
1840	    source_columns = table._columns
1841	    row_count = table.row_count
1842	    where = bound["where"]
1843	
1844	    if where is None:
1845	        selected = list(range(row_count))
1846	    else:
1847	        selected = [
1848	            i
1849	            for i in range(row_count)
1850	            if _eval(where, tuple(col[i] for col in source_columns)) is True
1851	        ]
1852	
1853	    if bound["mode"] == "plain":
1854	        return _run_plain(table, select, bound, selected)
1855	    return _run_aggregate(table, select, bound, selected)
1856	
1857	
1858	def _run_plain(table: Table, select: _Select, bound, selected: list[int]) -> Table:
1859	    items = bound["items"]
1860	    order_by = bound["order_by"]
1861	    source_columns = table._columns
1862	    # Execution order: WHERE (done by the caller) -> sort keys -> stable sort
1863	    # -> LIMIT -> result expressions, so rows filtered out or cut by LIMIT
1864	    # never evaluate the SELECT expressions.
1865	    if order_by is not None:
1866	        comparator = _make_row_comparator(source_columns, order_by, selected)
1867	        selected = sorted(selected, key=cmp_to_key(comparator))
1868	
1869	    if select.limit is not None:
1870	        selected = selected[: select.limit]
1871	
1872	    out_columns = []
1873	    out_schema_columns = []
1874	    for item in items:
1875	        if item.kind == "column":
1876	            out_columns.append(
1877	                tuple(source_columns[item.col_index][i] for i in selected)
1878	            )
1879	            out_schema_columns.append(table.schema.columns[item.col_index])
1880	        else:  # "expr"
1881	            out_columns.append(
1882	                tuple(
1883	                    _eval(item.expr, _row_values(source_columns, i))
1884	                    for i in selected
1885	                )
1886	            )
1887	            out_schema_columns.append(
1888	                ColumnSchema(item.output_name, item.out_type, nullable=item.nullable)
1889	            )
1890	    out_schema = Schema(out_schema_columns)
1891	    return Table._from_storage(out_schema, out_columns)
1892	
1893	
1894	def _run_aggregate(table: Table, select: _Select, bound, selected: list[int]) -> Table:
1895	    group_indices = bound["group_indices"]
1896	    bound_items = bound["items"]
1897	    order_by = bound["order_by"]
1898	    source_columns = table._columns
1899	
1900	    out_schema = Schema(
1901	        [
1902	            ColumnSchema(item.output_name, item.out_type, nullable=item.nullable)
1903	            for item in bound_items
1904	        ]
1905	    )
1906	
1907	    if group_indices:
1908	        groups = _build_groups(selected, source_columns, group_indices)
1909	    else:
1910	        # Without GROUP BY the whole filtered stream is the single group; an
1911	        # empty stream still produces the one all-NULL/COUNT-0 row.
1912	        groups = [tuple(selected)]
1913	
1914	    # Materialise one output tuple per group, following the SELECT order.
1915	    materialised: list[tuple] = []
1916	    for rows in groups:
1917	        values = []
1918	        for item in bound_items:
1919	            if item.kind == "column":
1920	                values.append(source_columns[item.col_index][rows[0]])
1921	            else:
1922	                values.append(
1923	                    _aggregate_value(
1924	                        item.func, item.arg_index, item.arg_type, rows, source_columns
1925	                    )
1926	                )
1927	        materialised.append(tuple(values))
1928	
1929	    if order_by is not None:
1930	        comparator = _make_tuple_comparator(materialised, order_by)
1931	        order = sorted(range(len(materialised)), key=cmp_to_key(comparator))
1932	    else:
1933	        order = list(range(len(materialised)))
1934	
1935	    if select.limit is not None:
1936	        order = order[: select.limit]
1937	
1938	    width = len(bound_items)
1939	    out_columns = [tuple(materialised[r][c] for r in order) for c in range(width)]
1940	    return Table._from_storage(out_schema, out_columns)
1941	
1942	
1943	def _build_groups(
1944	    selected: list[int],
1945	    source_columns: tuple[tuple, ...],
1946	    group_indices: tuple[int, ...],
1947	) -> list[tuple[int, ...]]:
1948	    groups: dict[tuple, list[int]] = {}
1949	    order: list[tuple] = []
1950	    for row_index in selected:
1951	        key = tuple(source_columns[col][row_index] for col in group_indices)
1952	        bucket = groups.get(key)
1953	        if bucket is None:
1954	            bucket = []
1955	            groups[key] = bucket
1956	            order.append(key)
1957	        bucket.append(row_index)
1958	    return [tuple(groups[key]) for key in order]
1959	
1960	
1961	def _row_values(source_columns: tuple[tuple, ...], i: int) -> tuple:
1962	    return tuple(col[i] for col in source_columns)
1963	
1964	
1965	def _make_row_comparator(
1966	    source_columns: tuple[tuple, ...],
1967	    order_by: tuple[tuple, ...],
1968	    selected: list[int],
1969	):
1970	    # Sort keys are computed for every row that passed WHERE, before the
1971	    # stable sort and LIMIT; expression keys (SELECT aliases) are evaluated
1972	    # here, so their errors surface even for rows LIMIT would cut.
1973	    key_sources: list[tuple] = []
1974	    for entry in order_by:
1975	        if entry[0] == "col":
1976	            key_sources.append((source_columns[entry[1]], entry[2], entry[3]))
1977	        else:  # "expr"
1978	            values = {
1979	                i: _eval(entry[1], _row_values(source_columns, i)) for i in selected
1980	            }
1981	            key_sources.append((values, entry[2], entry[3]))
1982	
1983	    def compare(a: int, b: int) -> int:
1984	        for values, descending, nulls_first in key_sources:
1985	            c = _compare_scalar(values[a], values[b], descending, nulls_first)
1986	            if c:
1987	                return c
1988	        return 0
1989	
1990	    return compare
1991	
1992	
1993	def _make_tuple_comparator(
1994	    rows: list[tuple],
1995	    order_by: tuple[tuple[int, bool, bool], ...],
1996	):
1997	    def compare(a: int, b: int) -> int:
1998	        for col_index, descending, nulls_first in order_by:
1999	            va = rows[a][col_index]
2000	            vb = rows[b][col_index]
2001	            c = _compare_scalar(va, vb, descending, nulls_first)
2002	            if c:
2003	                return c
2004	        return 0
2005	
2006	    return compare
2007	
2008	
2009	def _compare_scalar(va, vb, descending: bool, nulls_first: bool) -> int:
2010	    if va is None or vb is None:
2011	        if va is None and vb is None:
2012	            return 0
2013	        # NULL placement follows NULLS FIRST / NULLS LAST alone; the
2014	        # default (and the explicit LAST spelling) keeps NULLs at the
2015	        # end for both ASC and DESC, so DESC must not flip this part.
2016	        none_before = -1 if nulls_first else 1
2017	        return none_before if va is None else -none_before
2018	    c = (va > vb) - (va < vb)
2019	    return -c if descending else c
2020
